arxiv-2012-13581.title: Camouflaged Object Detection and Tracking: A Survey
arxiv-2012-13581.creator: Ajoy Mondal
arxiv-2012-13581.description: Abstract Moving object detection and tracking have various applications, including surveillance, anomaly detection, vehicle navigation, etc. The literature on object detection and tracking is rich enough, and several essential survey papers exist. However, the research on camouflage object detection and tracking is limited due to its complexity.

arxiv-2108-06486.title: Learning to Automatically Diagnose Multiple Diseases in Pediatric Chest Radiographs Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
arxiv-2108-06486.creator: Thanh T. Tran, Hieu H. Pham, Thang V. Nguyen, Tung T. Le, Hieu T. Nguyen, Ha Q. Nguyen
arxiv-2108-06486.description: Abstract Chest radiograph (CXR) interpretation is critical for the diagnosis of various thoracic diseases in pediatric patients. This task, however, is error-prone and requires a high level of understanding of radiologic expertise. Recently, deep convolutional neural networks (D-CNNs) have shown remarkable performance in interpreting CXR in adults.

arxiv-2211-09873.title: Randomised subspace methods for non-convex optimization, with applications to nonlinear least-squares
arxiv-2211-09873.creator: Coralia Cartis, Jaroslav Fowkes and Zhen Shao
arxiv-2211-09873.description: Abstract We propose a general random subspace framework for unconstrained nonconvex optimization problems that requires a weak probabilistic assumption on the subspace gradient, which we show to be satisfied by various random matrix ensembles, such as Gaussian and sparse sketching, using Johnson-Lindenstrauss embedding properties.

arxiv-2307-05154.title: Dynamic Rolling Horizon-Based Robust Energy Management for Microgrids Under Uncertainty
arxiv-2307-05154.creator: Jens Hönen, Johann L. Hurink, Bert Zwart
arxiv-2307-05154.description: Abstract Within the last few years, the trend towards more distributed, renewable energy sources has led to major changes and challenges in the electricity sector. To ensure a stable electricity distribution in this changing environment, we propose a robust energy management approach to deal with uncertainty occurring in microgrids.

arxiv-2410-10645.title: Macroscopic Quantum States and Universal Correlations in a Disorder-Order Interface Propagating over a 1D Ground State
arxiv-2410-10645.creator: Vanja Marić, Florent Ferro, Maurizio Fagotti
arxiv-2410-10645.description: Abstract We consider translationally invariant quantum spin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} chains with local interactions and a discrete symmetry that is spontaneously broken at zero temperature. We envision experimenters switching off the couplings between two parts of the system and preparing them in independent equilibrium states. One side of the chain settles into a symmetry-breaking ground state.

arxiv-2502-21223.title: The IDEA detector concept for FCC-ee
arxiv-2502-21223.creator: The IDEA Study Group
arxiv-2502-21223.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by The IDEA Study Group. A detector concept, named IDEA, optimized for the physics and running conditions at the FCC-ee is presented. After discussing the expected running conditions and the main physics drivers, a detailed description of the individual sub-detectors is given.

arxiv-2503-03972.title: RIS-enabled Multi-user M M -QAM Uplink NOMA Systems: Design, Analysis, and Optimization
arxiv-2503-03972.creator: Mahmoud AlaaEldin, Member, IEEE, Mohammad Al-Jarrah, Member, IEEE, Xidong Mu, Member, IEEE, Emad Alsusa, Senior Member, IEEE, Karim G. Seddik, Senior Member, IEEE, Michail Matthaiou, Fellow, IEEE
arxiv-2503-03972.description: Abstract Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is widely recognized for enhancing the energy and spectral efficiency through effective radio resource sharing. However, uplink NOMA systems face greater challenges than their downlink counterparts, as their bit error rate (BER) performance is hindered by an inherent error floor due to error propagation caused by imperfect successive interference cancellation (SIC).

arxiv-2503-22609.title: Quantum Entropy-Driven Modifications to Holographic Dark Energy in f ⁡ ( G , T ) f(G,T) Gravity
arxiv-2503-22609.creator: Giuseppe Gaetano Luciano
arxiv-2503-22609.description: Abstract In this work, we present a f ⁡ ( G , T ) f(G,T) gravity-based reconstruction of Barrow Holographic Dark Energy (BHDE). This approach extends the conventional HDE model by replacing the standard Bekenstein-Hawking entropy with Barrow entropy, which encapsulates quantum gravitational corrections to the geometry of black hole horizons.

arxiv-2508-03610.title: Density Estimation from Aggregated Data with Integrated Auxiliary Information: Estimating Population Densities with Geospatial Data
arxiv-2508-03610.creator: Michael Mühlbauer, Timo Schmid
arxiv-2508-03610.description: Abstract Density estimation for geospatial data ideally relies on precise geocoordinates, typically defined by longitude and latitude. However, such detailed information is often unavailable due to confidentiality constraints. As a result, analysts frequently work with spatially aggregated data, commonly visualized through choropleth maps.

arxiv-2510-00340.title: Modelling road mortality risks to persistence to a Western Toad ( Anaxyrus boreas ) population in British Columbia
arxiv-2510-00340.creator: Marguerite H. Mahr, Noah D. Marshall, Jessa Marley, Sarah K. Wyse, Wayne P. McCrory, Rebecca C. Tyson
arxiv-2510-00340.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Marguerite H. Mahr, Noah D. Marshall, Jessa Marley, Sarah K. Wyse, Wayne P. McCrory, Rebecca C. Tyson. Road mortality may be a significant factor in the global decline of amphibian populations, yet rigorous assessments of its effect on long-term population persistence are lacking. Here, we investigate population persistence through a field study and mathematical model of a western toad ( Anaxyrus Boreas (Baird and Girard, 1852) ) population within a highway corridor in the Selkirk Mountains of British Columbia.

pmc-10539518.title: A macroevolutionary common-garden experiment reveals differentially evolvable bone organization levels in slow arboreal mammals
pmc-10539518.creator: Fabio Alfieri, Léo Botton-Divet, Jan Wölfer, John A Nyakatura, Eli Amson
pmc-10539518.description: Eco-morphological convergence, i.e., similar phenotypes evolved in ecologically convergent taxa, naturally reproduces a common-garden experiment since it allows researchers to keep ecological factors constant, studying intrinsic evolutionary drivers. The latter may result in differential evolvability that, among individual anatomical parts, causes mosaic evolution.

pmc-10745384.title: A Rapid Prototyping Approach for Multi-Material, Reversibly Sealed Microfluidics
pmc-10745384.creator: Michael Halwes, Melanie Stamp, David J. Collins
pmc-10745384.description: Microfluidic organ-on-chip models recapitulate increasingly complex physiological phenomena to study tissue development and disease mechanisms, where there is a growing interest in retrieving delicate biological structures from these devices for downstream analysis. Standard bonding techniques, however, often utilize irreversible sealing, making sample retrieval unfeasible or necessitating destructive methods for disassembly.

pmc-12677946.title: Optimized DNA affinity purification sequencing determines relative binding affinity of transcription factors
pmc-12677946.creator: Katharina Schiller, Anja Meierhenrich, Sanja Zenker, Lennart M Sielmann, Bianca Laker, Andrea Bräutigam
pmc-12677946.description: DAP-seq is an in vitro method to analyze the relative binding affinity of transcription factors to DNA. It is a fast and scalable method and its application to plant transcription factors with a binary bound/not bound readout was first published in 2016 by O’Malley and colleagues.

pmc-12934335.title: Spontaneous intracranial artery dissection: risk factors, clinical features and imaging features
pmc-12934335.creator: Yidi Wang, Qingqing Jiang, Xiang Chen, Qiming Liang, Shiyi Cao, Furong Wang
pmc-12934335.description: PurposeThere remains a lack of epidemiological data and evidence regarding risk factors for intracranial arterial dissection (IAD) worldwide, making it difficult to make a more timely and accurate clinical diagnosis. We aimed to identify risk factors, clinical and imaging features of spontaneous IAD (sIAD) using a case-control design.

pmc-13092687.title: Comment on “Prevalence and risk factors of paediatric seizures in COVID-19 infection: A study from Thailand”
pmc-13092687.creator: Vidya Singaravelu, Amit Singh Pawaiya, Priyanka Aher, Hariharan Srinivasan

(a) In general The Pueblo shall have the following rights and interests in the Area: (1) Free and unrestricted access to the Area for traditional or cultural uses, to the extent that those uses are not inconsistent with— (A) the Wilderness Act.
